versions.codingNote: The highest credit-risk architecture is Score 4 because Choice funds Diversity and Veteran Incentive proceeds to franchisees through a 10-year or 5-year forgivable promissory note, a direct funded capital advance. Score 2 is also present because Choice may finance the affiliation fee via an interest-free promissory note, which is seller credit for a fee owed to Choice. The PMC, Direct Capital, Balboa, and Access Point arrangements are third-party financing programs with no disclosed franchisor guarantee or default exposure, making them Score 1; Choice receives flat annual payments but that is referral compensation, not credit risk. Selected capital support is discretionary and its instrument is unspecified, but it involves a commitment to return capital support. The Item 10 states Choice has not sold, assigned, or discounted its commercial paper, so no risk transfer is disclosed.

ITEM 10
                             FINANCING

may choose to extend financing for the Development Fee. The terms of repayment of the financing, such
as the number of monthly payments to be made, are negotiated on an individual basis depending on the
circumstances of the purchase and the total amount to be financed by us. A copy of the form of

        Typically, a down payment of between 60% and 70% of the Development Fee is made, and the
Promissory Note for the remainder is signed. The Security Agreement requires that a security in the AR
Business and all assets of the AR Business be pledged. The Promissory Note requires the accrual of
interest at an agreed upon rate of ten percent (10%) calculated monthly on the unpaid balance as of the
last day of each month.

      The Promissory Note must be signed by you and personally guaranteed by your owners (if you
are a legal entity). You must also pay all costs of collecting the amounts due under the Promissory Note,
including attorney fees. A default under the Promissory Note would be a default under the Franchise
Agreement and Area Representative Agreement, and may result in the termination of your Franchise
Agreement and Area Representative Agreement.   It is not our practice to sell, assign, or discount the
Promissory Note to a third party.

     We do not arrange any other type of financing from any other source.

===== PAGE 23 =====
ITEM 10
                              FINANCING

     MLHC may, at its discretion, make a line of credit available to franchisees for Initial
Franchise Fees, living expenses during training, equipment, lease build-out expenses and initial
working capital and start-up costs.  The rates on this loan will be the Wall Street Journal-
published Prime Rate, plus three percentage points per annum, depending on the credit profile
of the franchisee.  Interest will accrue but no principal or interest payments will be due during
training. You may make draws under the line of credit up to the opening of the Franchise Clinic.
The line of credit  will become due and payable in  full 90 days after the opening of your
Franchise Clinic. We may offer (or a third party affiliate may offer) to refinance the existing line
of credit through a term loan facility.  The loan will have a 5 year term with equal monthly
payments of principal and interest.  An origination fee of 5%  will be due and payable at
execution of the term loan documents and may be added to the existing balance. The rates on
these loans will typically be 10-20% per annum depending on the credit profile of the franchisee.
Prepayment is not permitted for the first three years of the loan term, after which time, you may
prepay with no penalty. MLHC and/or its affiliate will prepare all the necessary documents and
will handle the processing, payments, customer service, and collections according to standards
developed by us or our affiliate. Loans will be secured by Franchise Clinic equipment, signage,
decor, and inventory. A personal guarantee from the franchisee and his or her spouse will be
required. In the Franchise Agreement you will execute, you will waive your rights to certain
notices.  There are no waivers of defense in our promissory note, security agreement or
guaranty. If you are a legal entity, your shareholders, members, partners and/or owners must
personally guarantee the debt and agree to pay the entire debt and all collection costs. Should
a legal dispute arise, the franchisee agrees to waive the right to a jury trial and agrees not to
consolidate the action with others. A default on these loans will be considered a default under
the Franchise Agreement.  All loan participants will be required to permit electronic debiting of
accounts for payment. The financing documents are typically a Promissory Note, Security
Agreement, and Authorization for ACH Drafting of Loan Payments. MLHC reserves the right to
assign these loans to its affiliate or an unaffiliated third party. Any costs associated with the
assignment are the responsibility of the franchisee.  If you do not successfully complete the
training phase or fail to open a Franchise Clinic in the timeframe required in the Franchise
Agreement, the line of credit balance and accumulated interest will be due and payable 30 days
after termination of the Franchise Agreement.

DIVERSITY AND VETERAN INCENTIVE PROGRAM

     We  participate  in  the  International  Franchise  Association’s Veteran’s  Transition  Franchise
Initiative (known as VetFran®). We are currently offering a diversity and veteran incentive program to
encourage and increase the diversity of our franchise system and the hospitality industry as well as to
encourage entrepreneurs that have served in the United States military and been honorably discharged from
service (“Diversity and Veteran Incentive”). The Diversity and Veteran Incentive Program is intended to
attract top hotel developers from diverse backgrounds and involves our commitment of capital to
incentivize qualifying franchisees to develop either a newly constructed Choice-branded hotel or convert
an existing hotel to a Choice-branded hotel. Qualifying franchisees who enter into franchise agreements to
re-license Choice branded hotels that are currently part of the Choice franchise system are not eligible to
receive a Diversity and Veteran Incentive; however these franchisees will be given a 50% discount on the
then-current affiliation fee due in connection with the re-licensed franchise agreement (see below).

        Qualifications

      To qualify for the Diversity and Veteran Incentive Program, you must meet all of the following
conditions: you must request the Diversity and Veteran Incentive at the time of application; you must meet
our then-current qualifications for new franchisees (including our standard credit review); you must own
the hotel; if you are an individual, you must identify to us the characteristics and background that will
contribute to the diversity of our franchise system and the hospitality industry or if you are veteran you
must demonstrate that you have served in the United States military and have been honorably discharged
from service; or if you are a legal entity, you must be at least 51 % legally and beneficially owned by persons
that can demonstrate to us characteristics and background that will contribute to the diversity of our
franchise system and the hospitality industry or meet the requirements of a veteran stated above.  The
Diversity and Veteran Incentive Program may not be combined with any other incentive program that we
may be offering at the time of your application and we may discontinue the Diversity and Veteran Incentive
Program at any time.

        Incentive

       Each Diversity and Veteran Incentive we make for a hotel using the RODEWAY Marks will be for
$750 per room in the hotel (maximum of $50,000). Each incentive will be evidenced by a 10-year forgivable
promissory note (see Exhibit I) (the “Note”). We will pay the proceeds of the Note to you only after the
Opening Date of your hotel. You may use the proceeds of the Note for any purpose related to the hotel.
We do not require collateral for this Note, but may require personal guaranties, forgiveness of the Note
will be amortized over 10 years (beginning on the Opening Date of your hotel) using a straight-line method,
so that the Note will be completely forgiven if you do not commit certain defaults under the Note beginning
upon signing of the franchise agreement and ending 10 years after the Opening Date. The Note is structured
to provide for one payment at the end of 10 years; however, you do not have to make payments on the Note
if you remain in good standing under your franchise agreement. If you default in the obligations of franchise
agreement, your franchise agreement is terminated or expires, you die or you file for bankruptcy, then the
entire remaining unforgiven principal balance is immediately due along with interest (accruing on the
remaining unforgiven balance only) from the original date of the Note at an interest rate of prime plus 2%.
The maximum interest rate in California is 10% annually.   Under the Note, you must waive demand,
presentment for payment, protest, notice of dishonor and your right to a jury trial. On your default, you
also must pay all reasonable expenses, costs and attorneys’ fees that we incur in collecting the Note. The
Note contains no pre-payment penalty.

Your obligations under the Promissory Note are secured by security interest in all your assets that
you use in your Franchised Business. These assets include all equipment, inventory, agreements,
contracts, your Accounts, your accounts receivable, and all other property you now own or later
acquire, used in your Franchised Business. You may pay the Promissory Note early with no
prepayment penalty.   If you are a business entity, like a corporation or partnership, all your
owners must enter the Guaranty attached to the Unit Franchise Agreement. Under this Guaranty,
they guarantee that you will perform all your obligations under the Promissory Note.

If you default under the Promissory Note:
     the entire amount left on the Promissory Note becomes immediately due;
     you must pay court costs and legal fees we pay to collect the amounts you owe (even if
     we don’t sue you);
     you must pay interest at the lesser of (i) 18% a year or (ii) the maximum legal rate on the
       remaining principal balance, and all accrued interest; and
     we may terminate your Franchise Agreement.

Under the Promissory Note, you waive the following defenses and legal rights: valuation and
appraisement, demand, presentment, notice of non-payment, dishonor and protest; and your
right to a jury trial.

The Promissory Note permits us to assign it, but it is not our practice or current intention to sell,
assign, or discount all or any part of any Promissory Note to a third party.

Promissory Note in the form attached to the Franchise Agreement for the amount financed. A
summary of the other terms of the Promissory Note and Guaranty you must sign is disclosed
above. To qualify for this program, you must be a veteran who has received an honorable
discharge from the U.S. Military, and, you must give us a copy of your Form DD 214 showing your
status as a veteran.

===== PAGE 30 =====
Item 10.     FINANCING

       Fixtures and Furnishings for Traditional Stores.   If you develop a Traditional Store,
you will be allowed to pay us in installments for any furniture, fixtures, and fittings required in the
Store that are sold to you by us. The full price of these items will typically be between €185,000
and €210,000 ($207,200 - $235,200).  Installments will be due as follows: 45% of the total initial
price will be due upon the signing of the Franchise Agreement, but no later than 4 months
before the estimated opening of the Store; 40% of the total  initial price will be due upon the


G-Star FDD - 07/4§-(feV: ■Q-1/16)

===== PAGE 31 =====
estimated opening date of the Store; and the remaining 15% of the total initial price will be due 3
months after the actual opening date of the Store. The amounts of the first three installments
will be based on our estimate of the total amount, and the final installment will reflect the actual
amount, either in the form of a credit, or additional invoiced amount. No interest will be charged
on the unpaid amount as long as all payments are made as required.   If a payment is not made
when due, interest at the rate of 18% per annum or the maximum interest rate allowed by law
(whichever is less) will accrue from the due date to the date of payment.  Title to all furniture,
fixtures and fittings paid for under this installment plan will not pass to you (e.g., you will not own
it) until we have received the full price of all items. You may prepay the full amount at any time
without penalty.

       Inventory Payments. Your inventory costs will vary from Season to Season, depending
on several factors, including the size of your Store, your projected sales for the Season, the
specific items  in each Season’s collection and the previous success of your Store.  As an
example, we estimate that the cost of your initial inventory purchase will be between €400,000
and €880,000 ($448,000 - $985,600) for Traditional Stores and between €100,000 - €180,000
($112,000 - $201,600) for Q-Franchises.

      You may choose, for each Season, to pay your inventory expenses either in one lump
sum within 10 days of the invoice date, or in weekly installments following your receipt of the
invoices for a particular Season.  Each year, you must notify us no later than May  1^', for the
Fall/Winter season, and no later than November  1®', for the Spring/Summer season, regarding
your choice between payment options for the inventory for that Season.   If you choose to opt for
payment of all sums due in installments or you do not or fail to communicate your choice in time,
we shall issue a payment plan to allow you to pay part or  all of the sums due  in weekly
installments.

             If you operate a Q-Franchise, for your first delivery of Products only, which  will take
place at or prior to the opening of the Store, the payment plan  will have weekly payments
spread over a duration of 48 months.  For Q-Franchises, the payment plans for all subsequent
deliveries of Products in your first Season or any subsequent Season shall require the payment
of weekly installments over a duration of 6 months.

             If you operate a Traditional Store, we  will establish the terms and conditions of the
installment payment plan, in our sole discretion, and these terms and conditions may vary from
franchisee to franchisee and from Season to Season.  Payments  will be due weekly, and,
typically, the plan will be structured so that the full amount financed will be paid off before the
next season.

       Adjustments to the account will be made at the end of each Season to account for actual
shipments and returns during the Season. No interest will be charged on the unpaid amount as
long as all payments are made as required.   If any payment is not made when due under the
installment plan, we will be entitled to draw on the Bank Guarantee you are required to provide.
If any amounts remain past due, interest at the rate of 18% per annum or the maximum interest
rate allowed by law (whichever is less) will accrue from the due date to the date of payment.
Future inventory shipments will cease until the account is again current.  Title to all inventory
paid for under this installment plan will not pass to you (e.g., you will not own  it) until we have
received the full price of all items.  You may prepay the full amount due at any time, without
penalty.


G-Star FDD - 07/15 (reV:-Q1/16)
EAS-ni01611068.7l 7.4401997.4

===== PAGE 32 =====
If you  fail to comply with the payment plan that we issue for a particular Season, we
may, at our option and in our sole discretion, choose either (i) to demand immediate fulfillment
of the  entire payment  obligation,  in which case  all remaining  unpaid  installments  of the
obligations will become immediately due and payable, or  (ii) to require payment in advance of
the outstanding amount of the then-current Season and for future Seasons.

      Turnkey Installments for Q-Franchises.    If you develop a Q-Franchise on a turnkey
basis, you may pay us in 60 monthly installments for Turnkey Services and the Turnkey Goods
(collectively, the “Turnkey Expenses”), the Entrance Fee, the POS System cost, and the
Administration and Handling Fee (the “Turnkey Installments”).  The first Turnkey Installment
will be due on the earlier of (i) the last day of the calendar month following the opening of the
Store or  (ii) 90 days following the handover of the Store to you.  Each subsequent Turnkey
Installment shall be due on the last day of each calendar month following the due date of the
previous installment. No interest will be charged on the unpaid amount as long as all payments
are made as required.  At the expiration or termination  of the Franchise Agreement, any
outstanding balance of the Turnkey Installments will become immediately due for repayment to
us.   If you fail to make a Turnkey Installment by the applicable due date, we, upon written notice
to  you,  in our sole  discretion, may  also make any outstanding  balance  of the Turnkey
Installments immediately due for repayment to us and/or may require you to pay interest at the
rate of 18% per annum or the maximum interest rate allowed by law (whichever is less) from the
due date to the date of payment.  You may prepay the balance of any remaining Turnkey
Installments without penalty at any time.

         Until you have paid the Turnkey Expenses, the POS System cost, Administration and
Handling Fee, and Entrance Fee  in  full, you may not pay any management fees, director’s
salaries, or shareholder dividends in excess of the costs established  in the financial business
case that you must submit to us and that we must approve, and you must procure the consent
of our shareholders or members with respect to the limitation of dividend payments using a form
that we approve.

         All right,  title, and interest in the Turnkey Goods shall be owned exclusively by us until
the Turnkey Expenses are fully paid.    If the Franchise Agreement  is terminated prior to the
Turnkey Expenses being paid in full, (i) you will not receive a refund from us for any amount you
paid to us prior to the effective date of termination, nor will you be relieved of any monetary
obligations arising prior to the effective date of termination, and  (ii) all right, title, and interest in
the Turnkey Goods shall be retained by us, who shall have the right to permanently remove any
of the Turnkey Goods from the Premises without paying any compensation to you.

      Working Capital Loan for Q-Franchises.   If you develop a Q-Franchise, we may offer
you, at our sole discretion, a loan of working capital to assist you in paying  all or part of the
following: your first month of rent for the Store, the first month of payroll for the Store, and the
key money that you are required to pay to the landlord of the Store. You must repay the loan
with 5% interest  in 60 monthly installments at the same time that the Turnkey Installments
become due. At the expiration or termination of this Agreement, any outstanding balance of the
loan, including interest, will become immediately due for repayment to us.  If you fail to make a
loan payment by the applicable due date, we, upon written notice to you, in our sole discretion,
may also make any outstanding balance of the loan, including interest, immediately due for
repayment to us.  You may prepay the balance of the loan without penalty at any time.  You
must execute any documents that we require to evidence the terms of the loan. Until you have
repaid the loan, including interest,  in  full, you may not pay any management fees, director’s
salaries, or shareholder dividends in excess of the costs established in the financial business

F.ASTA101611068.7174401997.4

===== PAGE 33 =====
case that you must submit to us and that we must approve, and you must procure the consent
of our shareholders or members with respect to the limitation of dividend payments using a form
that we approve.

       Security Interests.  Pursuant to the Franchise Agreement and our General Terms and
Conditions of Sale, which are attached as Exhibit E to the Franchise Agreement that is attached
as Exhibit A to this Disclosure Document, we may require you to grant us a security interest in
the Collateral to secure the repayment of all amounts owing by you to us.   If we require you to
grant a security interest, you must execute a Purchase Money Security Agreement that  is
substantially  in the form attached as Exhibit G to the Franchise Agreement and any other
documents  required  by us  to  perfect our  security  interest.  You must use commercially
reasonable efforts to assist us in any way that we determine is necessary or advisable to perfect
our interest in the Collateral. We may file a UCC financing statement to perfect such security
interest, and we can enforce such security interest in inventory after you fail to pay in full any
amounts owing to us from time to time.

      Guarantees. Under the terms of the Payment and Performance Guarantees attached to
the Franchise Agreement and the Area Development Agreement,  if any, each individual with an
ownership interest in the franchisee,  if an entity, must personally guarantee the franchisee’s
obligations in connection with the payment plans described above. See Items 15 and 22.

         In addition,  if you develop a Q-Franchise you must warrant to us that you have at least
€50,000 ($56,000) in liquid assets in your personal accounts to use as working capital to fund
operating costs associated with the Store.  Upon our request, you must demonstrate that you
have maintained the required liquid assets or spent them on operating costs associated with the
Store.

       General. We do not intend to sell, assign or discount to a third party all or part of the
financing  arrangements  described  above.  We  and  our  affiliates  do  not  receive  any
consideration for placing any financing with any lender.

       Except as disclosed above, we and our affiliates do not offer direct or indirect financing
arrangements. We and our affiliates do not guarantee your note, lease or any other obligation.
